tools.name: studio_loop_status
tools.title: Loop status
tools.description: A loop's state: status, iteration, current stage, pending assignments (with prompts), per-iteration history (stage reports, playtests, filed feedback, verified effects) and metric trends. Without a loop name, lists every loop and the available templates.

tools.name: studio_loop_stop
tools.title: Stop loop
tools.description: Stop a running loop (pending assignments are dropped).

tools.name: studio_message_send
tools.title: Send message
tools.description: Talk to the team so the back-and-forth is visible: post in a channel (#general by default; any name creates a channel), address agents with `to` or @mentions in the text (@id, @role, @discipline, @all), reply in a thread with reply_to, and reference a task/feedback. Example: {text:"@lighting_artist the lava needs a stronger glow, see F-2", feedback:"F-2"}.

kind.description: Structured message kind for agent harnesses (default chat): request, inform, handoff, result, approval_request, approval_answer, ...

data.description: Structured payload for agent harnesses (the text stays the human-readable summary)

as.description: Act as this roster member (agent id). For external agents whose MCP client name isn't "<client>/<agent id>" (e.g. Claude Code subagents playing a role). Ignored when you already are one.

tools.name: studio_inbox
tools.title: Inbox
tools.description: Messages for you (addressed to you, mentioning you, or broadcast in #general), oldest first; unread only by default, and reading marks them read. Check it when you start a task. `channel` reads a whole channel; agent reads someone else's inbox without marking.

channel.description: Read this channel instead ("*" = every channel)

thread.description: Read a whole thread instead (root message id); never marks read

after.description: With channel or thread: only messages newer than this id

as.description: Act as this roster member (agent id). For external agents whose MCP client name isn't "<client>/<agent id>" (e.g. Claude Code subagents playing a role). Ignored when you already are one.

tools.name: playtest_run
tools.title: Playtest
tools.description: Play the game with a bot in a sandbox copy of the scene (the scene you edit is untouched) and get a report: completion rate, time-to-goal, deaths and their causes, fails, damage, stuck periods, objectives, coverage, frame cost, screenshots at notable moments and a top-down heatmap (returned as an image). Policies: goal_seeker (walks to entities tagged "goal"/"objective", avoids "hazard"/"enemy"), explorer (covers unexplored space), random, scripted (script: [{t: seconds, hold|release|press|click|event: ...}] — the same arguments as sim_input). persona {reaction_time, skill, curiosity, patience} shapes the bot; playtester agents use their own persona by default. runs>1 aggregates several seeds. Games should tag the player "player" and emit "death" / "fail" / "damage" / "objective" events. Saved under studio/playtests/<id>/; findings are returned for filing as feedback.

controls.description: Key mapping {up, down, left, right, jump} (default w/s/a/d/space)

goal_radius.description: Meters from a goal that count as reaching it (default 1)

as.description: Act as this roster member (agent id). For external agents whose MCP client name isn't "<client>/<agent id>" (e.g. Claude Code subagents playing a role). Ignored when you already are one.

tools.name: playtest_compare
tools.title: Compare playtests
tools.description: Before/after comparison of two playtests (ids like P-3): every metric with its delta and whether it got better or worse (direction-aware: fewer deaths is better, higher completion is better). Pass feedback to record the result as that feedback's measured effect: improved → verified, regressed → regressed (its tasks reopen). Timing metrics (*_ms, est_fps) depend on the machine's load, so they only decide the verdict for performance feedback or when a target names them; they are always listed.

feedback.description: Record the effect for this feedback item

as.description: Act as this roster member (agent id). For external agents whose MCP client name isn't "<client>/<agent id>" (e.g. Claude Code subagents playing a role). Ignored when you already are one.

tools.name: physics_add
tools.title: Make physical
tools.description: Make entities physical with a preset (one undoable edit). prop = dynamic rigid body with a collider fitted to its mesh and a mass estimated from its size; static_level = static colliders for every mesh under the entity (triangle-exact for imported models) — use on level roots; kinematic_platform = moved by its transform/scripts, carries and pushes things; player_character / npc_character = capsule character controller fitted to the mesh (drive with walk/jump in Wander); trigger_zone = sensor that fires `on trigger_enter`/`on trigger_exit`; debris = light, does not collide with characters; projectile = fast (continuous collision); remove = strip body/collider/character/joint. `overrides` patches the components, e.g. {"body": {"mass": 80, "restitution": 0.6}, "collider": {"shape": "sphere"}}. Example: {"entities": ["Crate 1", "Crate 2"], "preset": "prop"}.

tools.name: physics_query
tools.title: Physics query
tools.description: Ask the collision world (colliders, not render meshes) — works while editing and playing. raycast = first hit along a ray; raycast_all = every entity along it; shapecast = sweep a sphere/box/capsule (will this fit / where does it land?); overlap = entities touching a shape at `origin` (is this spot free?). Triggers are ignored unless include_triggers. Example: {"type": "raycast", "origin": [0, 10, 0], "direction": [0, -1, 0]}.

origin.description: Ray/sweep start, or the overlap shape center

tools.name: physics_settle
tools.title: Settle with physics
tools.description: Drop objects with a real simulation and keep where they come to rest (simulate, then keep the poses). Only the listed entities move (as dynamic bodies, even without a body component); everything else is frozen. The result is ONE undoable edit. Great after scatter/place: rocks, crates, books and debris end up naturally stacked and resting instead of floating or intersecting. Example: {"entities": ["Crate 1", "Crate 2", "Barrel"], "seconds": 4}.

seconds.description: Max simulated seconds (default 4, max 30); stops early when everything sleeps

freeze_others.description: Keep other dynamic bodies still (default true)

tools.name: physics_debug
tools.title: See colliders
tools.description: Capture the viewport with every collider drawn as a wireframe (color = state) plus physics stats (bodies, awake/asleep, contacts, triggers, characters, joints) and warnings (bad layers, unsupported shapes, missing joint targets). Use it to check that colliders match the visuals, triggers sit where you expect, and props fall asleep. view: editor (default), scene camera, or top (orthographic map).

tools.name: physics_settings
tools.title: Physics settings
tools.description: Read or change scene-wide physics: gravity (m/s^2), substeps (stability for stacks/fast objects), which collision layers ignore each other (ignorePairs, e.g. "debris-player, projectile-projectile"), sleeping, on/off. Stored in a `physics_world` component (created on an entity named "Physics" when you first change it). Example: {"gravity": [0, -1.62, 0]} for the Moon.

ignorePairs.description: Layer pairs that never collide, comma separated

tools.name: nav_build
tools.title: Bake navmesh
tools.description: Bake (or rebuild) the navigation mesh from static colliders and static meshes, save it to the project and record the settings in the scene's `navmesh` component (one undoable edit; creates an entity named "Navigation" if needed). Re-run after changing the level layout. Settings default to the navmesh component's: agent_radius (walls eroded by it), agent_height, max_climb (steps), max_slope (degrees), cell_size (precision). Entities tagged "nav_ignore" are left out. Then use nav_path / nav_debug, or nav agents and navigate() in Wander.

cell_size.description: Voxel size in m (default 0.2; smaller = more precise, slower)

path.description: Project-relative file (default: next to the scene, <scene>.navmesh)

tools.name: nav_path
tools.title: Find path
tools.description: Walking path on the navmesh between two points or entities (bakes the navmesh first if needed). Returns the corner points, the walking length, and whether the goal is reachable (partial = it is not; the path ends at the closest reachable point). Use to check that a level is traversable or to plan patrols. Example: {"from": "Player", "to": [12, 0, -4]}.

from.description: Start: [x, y, z] or an entity

to.description: Goal: [x, y, z] or an entity

tools.name: nav_debug
tools.title: See navmesh
tools.description: Top-down map of the level with the navmesh drawn over it (teal = walkable), nav agents (yellow dots) with their current paths, and optionally a test path between two points (orange). The fastest way to spot unreachable rooms, doorways too narrow for agents, and gaps. Bakes the navmesh first if needed.

focus.description: Frame this entity instead of the whole navmesh

from.description: Optional test path start: [x, y, z] or an entity

tools.name: animation_list
tools.title: List animations
tools.description: Skeleton and clips of a rigged model or animated character. With `entity`: its animator's library (clips with duration and rootSpeed in m/s for locomotion clips), controller (parameters, states), current state, recent animation events and warnings. With `model`: a .anim library or an imported .glb/.gltf. With neither: every animation library in the project. bones=true lists bone names (for bone_attach, layer masks, look-at). Example: {"entity": "Hero"}.

entity.description: Character with an animator (or a child of one)

model.description: Animation library (.anim) or rigged model (.glb/.gltf), project-relative

bones.description: Include the bone hierarchy (default: true for model, false for entity)

tools.name: animator_setup
tools.title: Set up animator
tools.description: Create a state machine controller (*.animctl.json) for a character and assign it. preset=locomotion (default) finds idle/walk/run/jump clips by name and builds: parameter `speed` (m/s) driving a 1D blend Idle -> Walk -> Run whose thresholds are the clips' real root speeds (feet don't slide when you set speed to the actual velocity), and if there is a jump clip a `jump` trigger with Jump -> back to locomotion. preset=clips: one state per clip, no transitions (drive with play_animation). Override clip choices with `clips` ({"idle": "Breathe", "run": "Sprint"}), or pass a full `controller` document (parameters, layers with states/blend/blend2d, transitions with "when" conditions like "speed > 0.1 and grounded", exit times, events, masks) — it is validated with did-you-mean errors. Then drive it from Wander: set_param(self, "speed", v), trigger(self, "jump"), play_animation(self, "Wave").

clips.description: Clip choice overrides: idle, walk, run, jump

controller.description: A full controller document instead of a preset

path.description: Where to save the controller (default: next to the library, <name>.animctl.json)

library.description: Animation library (.anim) if the character has none yet

root_motion.description: Move the character by its clips' root motion (default: unchanged)

tools.name: animation_preview
tools.title: Preview animation
tools.description: Render a character posed at a clip or state at given times (editor preview; the scene is not changed). Frames the character automatically (three_quarter / front / side / back) unless eye/target are given. times=[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75] returns a contact sheet of images — check walk cycles, attacks, hand poses, props attached to bones. While playing, captures the live pose instead. Example: {"entity": "Hero", "clip": "Run", "times": [0, 0.2, 0.4]}.

entity.description: The character (or any entity under its animator)

clip.description: Clip or state to show (default: what the animator plays by default)

times.description: Several times -> one image each (max 8), e.g. a walk cycle contact sheet

params.description: Controller parameters for the preview, e.g. {"speed": 2.5}

eye.description: Custom camera position (instead of automatic framing)

save_path.description: Also write the (first) PNG to this project-relative path

tools.name: animator_set
tools.title: Drive animator
tools.description: Set an animator's parameters and triggers, or play a state/clip with a crossfade — live while the simulation runs (same as Wander set_param / trigger / play_animation), or as the editor preview while editing. Also sets look_at (head/spine IK toward an entity; "" clears), the editor preview mode/time. Returns the animator state. Example: {"entity": "Hero", "params": {"speed": 3}, "trigger": "jump"}.

trigger.description: Trigger name or list of names

play.description: State or clip to crossfade to (editing: shown as the preview)

loop.description: Loop the played clip (default: the state's setting; clips play once and return)

look_at.description: Entity the head turns toward ("" = off)

preview_time.description: Editing: show the default state (or `play`) at this time without saving it (live scrubbing)

clear_preview.description: Remove a preview set by play / preview_time while editing

tools.name: bone_attach
tools.title: Attach to bone
tools.description: Make an entity follow a bone of an animated character: a sword in the right hand, a hat on the head, a lantern on the hip. Validates the bone (did-you-mean; animation_list bones=true lists them), adds the `attach` component and (by default) parents the entity under the character. offset/rotation are in the bone's space. Example: {"entity": "Sword", "to": "Hero", "bone": "RightHand", "offset": [0, 0.08, 0.02]}.

bone.description: Bone name, e.g. RightHand, Head, mixamorig:Spine2

parent.description: Parent the prop under the character (default true)

tools.name: bone_ik
tools.title: Reach with IK
tools.description: Make a character's hand or foot reach a point with two-bone IK (the elbow/knee and shoulder/hip bend; bone lengths are kept): a hand on a door handle, rail or lever, a foot planted on a step. Either give `entity` (an existing object becomes the effector — the bone reaches it) or a `position` (a new effector entity is created under the character; default: where the bone is now). Move or keyframe the effector (sequence_key transform.position) to animate the reach; `weight` blends with the animation. pole = bend direction in the character's space ([0,0,-1] knees forward; elbows usually [0,0,1]). Example: {"character": "Hero", "bone": "RightHand", "entity": "Door Handle"}.

bone.description: End bone: LeftHand, RightHand, LeftFoot, RightFoot...

entity.description: Existing entity to reach (it gets the ik component)

position.description: World position for a new effector entity

name.description: Name of the new effector (default "<bone> IK")

pole.description: Bend direction in the character's space (default: keep the animated bend)

match_rotation.description: Also orient the bone like the effector (default false)

tools.name: sequence_create
tools.title: Create sequence
tools.description: Create a cinematic sequence asset (*.sequence.json) and an entity whose `sequencer` plays it when the simulation starts. Then add content with sequence_key (keyed properties, camera cuts, events, animations) and sequence_camera_shot (orbit / dolly / crane / track / pan / static / path / flyover moves), check frames with sequence_scrub and play with sequence_play. `tracks` may hold a full track list (see docs/ANIMATION.md). Example: {"path": "cinematics/intro.sequence.json", "duration": 10}.

duration.description: Length in seconds (0 = until the last key)

entity.description: Entity to play it: an existing one gets the sequencer, a new name creates it (default: a new entity named after the sequence)

tools.name: sequence_key
tools.title: Key sequence
tools.description: Add or replace keys in a sequence, many at once. `keys`: property keys {entity, property, t, value, ease} animating any component field ("transform.position", "transform.rotation", "light.intensity", "light.color", "camera.fov", "mesh.color", "mesh.emissive", "particles.rate", or "environment.sunElevation" without entity). ease: linear (default), step, smooth, ease_in, ease_out, auto (smooth spline through neighbours — best for camera paths) or [x1,y1,x2,y2] cubic-bezier. `camera_cuts`: [{t, camera}] which camera is live. `events`: [{t, event, target?}] Wander events. `animations`: [{entity, t, play, fade?, loop?, params?}] drive animators. A key at an existing time replaces it; replace=true clears touched tracks first. Example: {"sequence": "cinematics/intro.sequence.json", "keys": [{"entity": "Sun", "property": "light.intensity", "t": 0, "value": 0}, {"entity": "Sun", "property": "light.intensity", "t": 3, "value": 4, "ease": "smooth"}]}.

sequence.description: Sequence path (.sequence.json) or an entity with a sequencer

keys.description: Property keys {entity, property, t, value, ease}

animations.description: Animation keys {entity, t, play, fade, loop, params}

replace.description: Clear every touched track before adding (default false: merge)

tools.name: sequence_camera_shot
tools.title: Camera shot
tools.description: Add a procedural camera move to a sequence — the quickest way to direct cinematics. Shots are evaluated live each tick, so they follow moving targets. Kinds: orbit (around target; radius, height, from/to degrees), dolly (distance [far, near] along angle, or from/to points), crane (height [low, high]), track (side-on, slides from/to meters while following the target), pan (fixed position, look from/to: entities, points or yaw degrees), static (position looking at target), path (Catmull-Rom through points, looking at target or along the path), flyover (straight aerial pass over the target from the angle side: distance = half the pass length, height). fov: number or [from, to] (zoom), roll in degrees, ease (default smooth). cut=true (default) also switches to this camera at start. Missing cameras are created. Example: {"sequence": "Intro", "camera": "Cam A", "shot": "orbit", "target": "Hero", "start": 0, "duration": 5, "radius": 5, "height": 1.8, "from": -30, "to": 60}.

sequence.description: Sequence path or entity with a sequencer

camera.description: Camera entity (created if missing; default "Shot Camera")

start.description: Start time in seconds (default: after the camera's previous shot)

target.description: Entity name or [x,y,z] the camera frames

offset.description: Added to the target point (e.g. [0, 1.6, 0] for eye height)

height.description: Camera height above the target: number or [from, to]

distance.description: Distance from the target: number or [from, to]

fov.description: Field of view: number or [from, to] (zoom)

cut.description: Switch to this camera at start (default true)

tools.name: sequence_get
tools.title: Inspect sequence
tools.description: A sequence's tracks (type, entity, property, key count and time span) and length; with `time`, the evaluated property values and live camera at that moment.

sequence.description: Sequence path or entity with a sequencer

tools.name: sequence_play
tools.title: Play sequence
tools.description: Play or stop a sequence. Sequences run in the simulation: while editing this starts the simulation (like sim_control play) and plays the sequence from `from`; while playing it restarts / seeks or stops it. Sequencers with playOnStart start by themselves when the simulation starts. Watch with viewport_capture view="scene" after sim_control step.

sequence.description: Entity with a sequencer, or a sequence path played by one

tools.name: sequence_scrub
tools.title: Scrub sequence
tools.description: Look at a sequence at any time without playing: renders through the sequence's live camera (cuts and shots) with every keyed property and animation applied, then restores the scene. times=[...] returns up to 8 images (a storyboard). Render a whole shot to disk with fps + from/to + save_dir (PNG frames, e.g. for a video). persist=true instead leaves the editor showing that time (sequencer preview). Only while editing. Example: {"sequence": "Intro", "times": [0, 2.5, 5]}.

sequence.description: Entity with a sequencer, or a sequence path played by one

fps.description: Render frames at this rate between from and to into save_dir

to.description: Render range end (default: the sequence length)

camera.description: Look through the sequence's camera (default) or the editor camera

persist.description: Keep showing this time in the editor (sets sequencer preview/time)

include_image.description: Return the images (default true; false = just render / save)

transient.description: Only show `time` in the editor viewport (no capture, not saved) until clear

tools.name: groom_create
tools.title: Create hair or fur
tools.description: Grow strand hair or fur on an entity's mesh (a head, a bust, an animal body) from a preset, ready to tweak. Presets: hair_straight, hair_wavy, hair_curly, hair_ponytail, hair_short (heads: they grow on the upper back of the mesh; set maskDirection/maskAngle or a vertex-color mask for your model), fur_short, fur_long (cover the whole mesh). `overrides` patches groom fields, e.g. {"melanin": 0.2, "length": 0.5, "strands": 100000}. Color is physically based: melanin 0 white .. 0.3 blond .. 0.8 brown .. 1 black, redness for auburn/ginger, dye for unnatural tints. Hair is simulated (gravity, wind, collisions with the mesh) and rendered as real strands with Marschner shading and self-shadowing. Example: {"entity": "Head", "preset": "hair_wavy", "overrides": {"melanin": 0.25}}.

entity.description: Entity with the mesh to grow on (gets the groom component)

tools.name: groom_update
tools.title: Update hair or fur
tools.description: Change a groom's fields (or switch to another preset and then apply `fields`). Geometry fields (strands, length, curls, clumps, mask...) regenerate the strands; color, shading and motion fields apply instantly. Example: {"entity": "Head", "fields": {"curlRadius": 0.01, "curlFrequency": 18, "melanin": 0.9}}.

tools.name: groom_info
tools.title: Hair or fur info
tools.description: Strand, guide and point counts, memory (CPU and GPU), generation time and the measured GPU cost (simulation and drawing) of a groom, or of every groom in the scene when `entity` is omitted. Use it to budget hair (e.g. keep a hero head under ~2 ms at 1080p).

entity.description: Entity with a groom (omit for all)

tools.name: groom_export
tools.title: Export groom strands
tools.description: Write a groom's rest-pose strands to a file for DCC round trips: .hair (Cem Yuksel's format, read by many hair tools), .groom.json (readable) or .skygroom (compact binary). Paths are project-relative.

tools.name: fx_benchmark
tools.title: Benchmark GPU frame time
tools.description: Render `frames` real-time frames back to back (no readback, effects time advancing 1/60 s per frame, so GPU particles and hair simulate) and report the GPU time per frame and per effects pass, plus the wall-clock time. Use it to budget effects: e.g. {"width":1920,"height":1080,"frames":120}. The view is the editor camera unless eye/target are given.

serial.description: Wait for each frame (default true): exact per-pass GPU times; false = frames overlap like a game loop (throughput)

tools.name: fx_stats
tools.title: GPU effects stats
tools.description: Measured GPU cost of the last rendered frames: whole-frame GPU time, the GPU simulation pass (particles + hair), per-emitter live particle counts (read back asynchronously, a few frames old) and per-groom sizes. Render a few frames (viewport_capture) first; values are 0 on renderers without GPU effects.

tools.name: impostor_bake
tools.title: Bake foliage impostors
tools.description: Bake the octahedral impostors of foliage layers now: each heavy model (an imported tree, bush, rock or grass clump; one mesh or every part of a prefab) is captured from up to 32x32 directions into an atlas of albedo, normal and depth, and instances beyond the layer's transition distance render as impostors (lit, shadowed and depth-correct like real geometry). The renderer bakes on first use and caches in .skywalker/cache/impostors/, so this is for baking ahead of time, rebaking after editing a mesh or material (rebake:true), or checking the atlases (preview:true returns the first atlas as an image). Tune per layer with impostorDistance (m; 0 auto from on-screen size, -1 off), impostorResolution (atlas px) and impostorFrames (views per side); see the transition distance in the result. Example: {"entity":"Forest","layer":0,"rebake":true,"preview":true}.

entity.description: Foliage entity (default: every foliage entity in the scene)

layer.description: Layer index or name (default: every layer)

rebake.description: Bake again even when a cached atlas exists (default false)

preview.description: Return the first atlas as an image (default false)

save_preview.description: Also write that preview PNG to this project-relative path

tools.name: game_settings
tools.title: Game settings (game.json)
tools.description: Read or change the project's shipping settings in game.json: startScene, window {width,height,fullscreen,resizable,vsync}, quality (low|medium|high|ultra), renderScale, quitOnEscape, pauseOnFocusLoss, icon (a PNG, 1024x1024 recommended), bundleId (reverse-DNS), version, copyright, plus include/exclude globs for packaging, and the description fields (id, title, genre, mood, pitch), and mounts: shared folders outside the project addressed by a top-level name, e.g. {"mounts": {"kit": "../_kit"}} makes kit/characters/guard.prefab.json resolve into ../_kit (assets, prefabs, materials and animations load from it; game_build copies what the game uses). `get` returns the effective settings, the resolved start scene and validation problems. `set` merges the given fields (null removes one) and validates them. Example: {"operation":"set","settings":{"title":"Sky Dash","startScene":"scenes/main.sky.json","window":{"width":1280,"height":720}}}

settings.description: Fields to merge into game.json (set only)

tools.name: game_build
tools.title: Build the game as a macOS app
tools.description: Package the project as a standalone macOS app (Name.app): the player runtime, the scenes, the assets they reference (computed from scenes, prefabs, materials and Wander scripts; all_assets ships everything), scripts, the project's native module (compiled now), Info.plist, an icon made from the game.json icon, and an ad-hoc code signature. Settings come from game.json (see game_settings). Returns the app path, size, file count by type, and warnings (missing assets, no icon). dry_run reports what would ship without writing anything. The app runs on this Mac; distributing it needs a Developer ID signature and notarization (docs/SHIPPING.md). Example: {"out":"/Users/me/Builds","release":true}

out.description: Folder to write <Name>.app into (outside the project is best; ~/Desktop, ~/Builds)

icon.description: PNG path (absolute or project-relative); overrides game.json icon

release.description: Strip the player's symbols for a smaller app (default false)

all_assets.description: Ship every asset in the project, not only referenced ones (use when scripts build paths at run time)

annotations.title: Build the game as a macOS app

tools.name: game_run
tools.title: Run the game in the standalone player
tools.description: Start the standalone player on the current project as a separate process to try the game like a player would (real window, real input, audio). It runs the saved scene file (save first); without `scene` it uses the open scene or game.json's start scene. Returns the pid and a log file. `status` shows whether it is still running and its recent output; `stop` ends it. With `capture` the player renders one frame to a PNG after `frames` frames and exits (a screenshot of the real player output). `seconds` closes the game by itself. `app` runs a built .app instead. Example: {"action":"start","scene":"scenes/level2.sky.json","width":1280} or {"capture":"/tmp/shot.png","frames":120}

scene.description: Scene to start in (project-relative); default: the open scene

app.description: Run this built .app instead of the project

capture.description: Write one frame to this PNG and quit

frames.description: With capture: frames to run before the capture (default 90)

wait.description: Wait for the player to exit and return its output (default true with capture/seconds)

annotations.title: Run the game in the standalone player

tools.name: movie_render
tools.title: Render movie
tools.description: Render a cinematic to video or a PNG sequence, offline and deterministically (the movie renderer). Renders a sequence (`sequence`: its entity or .sequence.json, whole length or start/end), an inline camera move (`camera`: {keys: [{t, eye, target, fov?, roll?}]} splined, or {shots: [{shot: orbit|dolly|crane|track|pan|static|path|flyover, duration, target, ...sequence_camera_shot fields}]} where each shot is a cut), or the scene camera for `duration` seconds. Always starts from the scene state and restores it after. simulate=true runs the game (scripts, physics); false (default) runs only sequences, animators and particles. Motion blur: `shutter` 0..1 of the frame (0.5 = 180 degrees; default the camera's motionBlur) accumulates sub-frames at fractional times; `samples` (default 8) is the per-frame budget. Outputs by extension: .mp4 = H.264 (codec hevc = 10-bit HEVC), .mov = ProRes 422 HQ, a folder or name_####.png = PNG sequence (resume=true continues an interrupted one). clay=true / debug_view="sketch" render the same move as clay or pencil sketch. Blocks until done and returns frames, timings and paths; background=true returns at once (progress: movie_progress events, action="status"; action="cancel" stops). Example: {"sequence": "Intro", "output": "renders/intro.mp4", "resolution": "1080p", "fps": 24, "shutter": 0.5, "samples": 16}.

action.description: render (default), status of the current/last render, or cancel it

sequence.description: Sequence to render: entity with a sequencer, or a .sequence.json path

camera.description: Inline camera move: {keys: [{t, eye, target, fov?, roll?, ease?}]} or {shots: [{shot, duration, target, t?, ...}]}, plus aperture, focus_distance, tilt_shift

camera_entity.description: Look through this camera instead of the scene's primary one

simulate.description: Run the full game simulation (scripts, physics) while rendering (default false)

start.description: Start time in seconds (default 0; the simulation pre-rolls to it)

end.description: End time in seconds (default: the sequence / camera path length)

duration.description: Seconds to render from start (instead of end)

samples.description: Samples per frame (default 8; 16-32 for finals): anti-aliasing, noise-free GI, motion blur

shutter.description: Motion blur: open shutter as a fraction of the frame (0.5 = 180-degree film look, 0 = off)

shutter_samples.description: Sub-frames across the shutter (default: one per sample)

shutter_timing.description: Shutter interval relative to the frame time (default center)

quality.description: Render quality tier (default full; fast for previews)

clay.description: Matte clay look (same move, for sketch -> clay -> final transitions)

debug_view.description: Buffer visualization, shading debug view (wireframe, lod, unshaded, ...) or the pencil sketch look; see viewport_capture

warmup.description: Frames rendered before the first one so temporal effects settle (default 4)

output.description: Output path: .mp4 (H.264), .mov (ProRes 422 HQ), or a folder / name_####.png (PNG sequence); default renders/<name>.mp4

outputs.description: Several outputs from one render, e.g. ["renders/a.mp4", {"path": "renders/a.mov", "codec": "prores"}]

codec.description: Codec for `output`: h264, hevc (10-bit), prores (422 HQ), prores4444, png

bitrate_mbps.description: H.264 / HEVC average bitrate (default: chosen from size and fps)

resume.description: PNG sequences: continue from the first missing frame of an interrupted render

name.description: Name for reports and the default output path

background.description: Return immediately; the editor keeps rendering frame by frame (default false)

tools.name: render_layers
tools.title: Render layers and cull masks
tools.description: Render layers (20): MeshRenderer.layers says which layers a mesh is on; Camera.cullMask and Light.cullMask say which layers a camera draws and a light illuminates (a mesh is drawn / lit when they share a layer). Name layers in game.json and use the names everywhere. action get (default): named layers, meshes per layer, cameras and lights with restricted masks, plus warnings (meshes no camera sees, lights that light nothing). action name: {layer: 2, name: "player"} (name "" clears). action set: {entities, layers} puts meshes on layers and/or {entities, cull_mask} sets cameras' and lights' masks; masks accept a number (raw bits), a layer name, "3", "all", "none" or a list; mode add/remove edits the existing mask instead of replacing it. Uses: a rim light only on the hero ({entities:["RimLight"], cull_mask:"hero"}), first-person arms hidden from a mirror camera, editor-only helpers on layer 20 hidden from the game camera. Example: {"action":"set","entities":["Hero"],"layers":["world","hero"]}

action.description: get (default), name a layer, or set masks

name.description: name: the layer's name ("" removes it)

layers.description: set: the meshes' layers (number, name, "all", or a list of names / layer numbers)

cull_mask.description: set: the cameras' / lights' cull mask (same forms as layers)

mode.description: set: replace the mask (default), add layers to it, or remove them

tools.name: process_info
tools.title: Pause, time scale and smoothing
tools.description: What runs while the game is paused or slowed, and how smooth real-time frames are. Reports the game clock (paused?, time scale, game vs real time), every entity with a `process` component or a UI canvas (UI runs `always` by default), and with `entity` that entity's effective settings and WHY (which ancestor decided its mode). Also render interpolation: alpha, entities smoothed last frame, `on frame` handler runs and frame pacing jitter (jitterMs vs jitterMsWithoutInterpolation). Warnings flag a paused game nothing can resume. Example: {"entity": "PauseMenu"}.

entity.description: Entity to explain (effective mode, clock, interpolation, whether it runs from the next tick)

tools.name: sim_teleport
tools.title: Teleport entity
tools.description: Move an entity instantly — a respawn, a portal, a checkpoint — without render interpolation smearing it across the screen for a frame (Wander: teleport(entity, position)). position/rotation are local (like transform). Without position/rotation it only resets the smoothing. Undoable.

tools.name: shadow_atlas_info
tools.title: Inspect point/spot light shadows
tools.description: Which point and spot lights cast shadows this frame and how: projection (spot view, cube = 6 views, dual_paraboloid = 2 views), atlas slot and resolution, whether it was re-rendered this frame or reused from the static cache, and why a light has no shadow (disabled, out_of_view, beyond_max_distance, over_light_budget, atlas_full, pending). Also the atlas size and memory, slots used per quadrant, the per-frame budgets (Environment.localShadowLights / localShadowUpdates) and warnings. Renders one real-time frame of `view` first (default: the editor camera). Use it when light leaks through walls, a shadow is missing or blocky, or to check the cost of many lamps; see the atlas itself with viewport_capture debug_view "shadow_atlas". With `entity`, also lists the meshes that block that light (casters, first 40) and the small fixtures right at the light that are ignored (lamp heads, bulbs). invalidate=true re-renders every cached shadow on the next frame. Example: {"view": "scene"} or {"entity": "Street Lamp 3"}.

view.description: Camera of the frame to inspect: "editor" (default), "scene", or {eye: [x,y,z], target: [x,y,z], fov: degrees}

render.description: Render a frame of `view` first (default true; false = the last frame rendered)

invalidate.description: Force every cached shadow to re-render (after editing meshes outside the engine, or to measure the full cost)

tools.name: light_shadows
tools.title: Configure light shadows
tools.description: Turn shadows of point/spot lights on or off and tune them, for one light, a list, or every light ("all", optionally only one kind). Shadows stop light leaking through walls and floors; they cost an atlas slot (cube point light = 6 views, spot = 1) but are cached while nothing in range moves. Tuning: resolution (slot px hint: 256 small, 1024 hero light; 0 = automatic), mode (cube | dual_paraboloid for cheaper point lights), bias (m; raise against speckled self-shadowing, lower if shadows float), normal_bias (texels), max_distance (m from the camera beyond which the shadow fades out). One undo step. Example: {"lights": "all", "kind": "point", "enabled": true, "max_distance": 40}.

lights.description: A light entity (id or name), a list of them, or "all"

kind.description: With "all": only lights of this kind

resolution.description: Atlas slot hint in px (0 = automatic, 128..2048)

max_distance.description: Camera distance (m) where the shadow fades out (0 = no limit)

tools.name: probe_add
tools.title: Add a reflection probe
tools.description: Add a reflection probe: a captured cubemap that glossy floors, metal and glass inside its volume reflect instead of the sky (box-projected, so reflections line up with the walls), and that gives them their ambient light. Put one per room, corridor or street section, with the capture point in open space at about eye height. size "auto" (default) casts rays from `position` to the nearest meshes in the six axis directions and fits the box to the room (open directions get 8 m): the volume reaches blend_distance past the walls and the reflections project onto the room (projectionSize); or give [x, y, z] in meters. interior=true for closed rooms: no sky light leaks in (the probe replaces it; windows still show the sky). update: once (default, cached until it moves or probe_bake), on_change (re-captures when something in range changes), realtime (every `interval` frames, within Environment.probeUpdates faces per frame). The new probe is captured right away and its state returned (see probe_info). Example: {"name": "Hall Probe", "position": [0, 1.6, 0], "interior": true}.

position.description: Capture point in meters (the room's open space, ~1.5 m up)

size.description: Box size [x, y, z] in meters, or "auto" (default): fit the room around `position`

interior.description: Closed room: no sky light inside (default false)

blend_distance.description: Meters over which the probe fades at its edges (default 1)

box_projection.description: Parallax-correct reflections against the box (default true)

ambient.description: Diffuse ambient inside the volume (default probe)

cull_mask.description: Render layers the capture draws: names, numbers, "all" (default) or a list

render.description: Capture it now and return its state (default true)

tools.name: probe_bake
tools.title: Re-capture reflection probes
tools.description: Re-capture reflection probes now (after moving furniture, changing lights or the sky): renders one still frame of `view`, which captures every invalidated probe in full regardless of the per-frame face budget, and returns their state (slot, captures, GPU time) plus warnings. probes: one entity, a list or "all" (default). render=false only marks them; they re-capture over the next frames (Wander: probe_bake()). Example: {"probes": ["Hall Probe"]}.

probes.description: A probe entity, a list of them, or "all" (default)

view.description: Camera of the frame: "editor" (default), "scene", or {eye, target, fov}

render.description: Render the frame that captures them now (default true)

tools.name: probe_info
tools.title: Inspect reflection probes
tools.description: Reflection probes and their atlas: the budget (Environment.probeBudget probes, probeUpdates faces per frame), atlas resolution / slots / memory, and per probe: slot and debug color (the reflection_probes debug view draws it), whether it is captured, lighting this view, waiting for the face budget, over budget or out of view, captures so far, last capture GPU time, `stale` (something in range changed since a once probe was captured: run probe_bake), size, update mode. Warnings: overlapping volumes with equal priority, probes with no geometry in them, capture points inside a mesh, atlas exhaustion. Renders one real-time frame of `view` first. See the volumes with viewport_capture {debug_view: "reflection_probes"} and a probe's cubemap with viewport_capture {probe: "Hall Probe"}. Example: {"entity": "Hall Probe"}.

view.description: Camera of the frame: "editor" (default), "scene", or {eye, target, fov}

render.description: Render a frame of `view` first (default true; false = the last frame)

tools.name: entity_refs
tools.title: Entity references
tools.description: Who references an entity and what it references (joint targets, camera follow, look-at, bone attachments, IK, groom/particle colliders...). Links store the target's id plus its name, so they survive renames. Without `entity`: a scene-wide health check listing dangling links (pointing at nothing), links that only resolve by name (fragile), duplicate unique names and broken prefab instances, each with a fix. Example: {"entity": "Door"} before renaming or deleting it.

entity.description: Entity to inspect; omit for the scene-wide check

tools.name: entity_copy
tools.title: Copy entities
tools.description: Copy entities (with children) to a clipboard document for entity_paste — in this scene or after scene_load in another. Links between copied entities and prefab instances inside the copy are kept.

entities.description: Entities to copy (their children come along)

tools.name: entity_paste
tools.title: Paste entities
tools.description: Create copies of a clipboard document from entity_copy. Links among the pasted entities point at the new copies (a pasted rig stays wired to itself); links to other entities keep their target; prefab instances stay linked. Optional parent and position offset.

parent.description: Parent of the pasted roots (default: none)

offset.description: Added to each pasted root's position

tools.name: prefab_overrides
tools.title: Prefab overrides
tools.description: How a linked prefab instance differs from its prefab: per-field overrides (with the prefab's value), removed nodes, added entities and its placement (root name/transform, never applied). `entity` may be the instance root or any entity inside it. Without `entity`: every instance in the scene with its override count. Then use prefab_revert to undo overrides or prefab_apply to push them into the prefab file.

entity.description: An instance root or member; omit to list all instances

prefab.description: Only instances of this prefab (path) when listing

tools.name: prefab_revert
tools.title: Revert prefab overrides
tools.description: Undo overrides so an instance matches its prefab again. `property` reverts one override of `entity` ("light.intensity", "name", "vars.hp", "collider" for an added/removed component); without it, all of that entity's overrides (placement kept). `all`: true reverts the whole instance and restores removed nodes (added entities stay). Undoable.

property.description: One override to revert, as listed by prefab_overrides

tools.name: prefab_apply
tools.title: Apply overrides to prefab
tools.description: Push an instance's overrides into its prefab file so every instance (in all scenes) gets them. Without `property`: everything — overrides, removed nodes and added entities (they become prefab nodes and stay linked). With `property`: only that override of `entity`. Placement (root name/transform) is never applied. Other instances in this scene update immediately and keep their own overrides. Undo restores the scene; the file keeps the new version (re-apply or edit to change it back).

tools.name: prefab_unpack
tools.title: Unpack prefab instance
tools.description: Make an instance local: its entities stay exactly as they are but are no longer linked to the prefab (edits to the prefab stop reaching it, and the scene saves it in full); also known as "make local". Undoable.

tools.name: prefab_relink
tools.title: Relink prefab copies
tools.description: Link existing copies of a prefab (made before prefabs were linked, or by copying entities) back to it. A candidate links when its hierarchy matches the prefab node for node (same child names in order) and it has at most `max_overrides` differences besides placement; values are never changed (differences become overrides). Without `entities` the whole scene is searched. dry_run reports without linking.

max_overrides.description: Most differences allowed (default 0: exact copies only)

dry_run.description: Only report what would be linked

tools.name: legal_info
tools.title: Legal documents and acceptance
tools.description: Skywalker's Terms of Use, Privacy Notice and license: their versions and effective dates, MCP resource URIs (skywalker://docs/legal/TERMS, skywalker://docs/legal/PRIVACY, skywalker://docs/LICENSING), whether a person has accepted the current versions on this computer (status current, outdated, not_recorded), and a verified summary of data practices (no telemetry; data leaves the computer only to the AI provider or download URL the human chose). Use it to answer licensing or privacy questions, or before advising on shipping. `document` (terms, privacy, license, licensing) adds that document's full text. Nothing waits for acceptance; a person accepts in the editor or with `skywalker legal --accept`, never an agent. Example: {"document": "privacy"}.

document.description: Include this document's full text: terms, privacy, license (the LICENSE file) or licensing (plain-language summary and third-party notices)

tools.name: tool_define
tools.title: Define a custom tool
tools.description:
Create or update your OWN tool when no engine tool does what you need. Kinds: "wander" — Wander code `fn run(args) ... end` that queries the scene and calls allowlisted tools (call_tool) under an instruction budget; "composite" — a pipeline of tool calls with templated args ({{args.x}}, {{steps.find.entities}}), for_each loops and a result mapping. Declare capabilities (read_scene, mutate, calls, files) as a minimal allowlist and add tests (args -> expect) — they run as dry runs before saving. Read-only tools become callable at once (as user_<name>, listed in tools/list); tools that mutate or write files wait for a human's approval (tool_approve) under the default policy. Updating merges your fields over the current definition. Example: {"name":"enemies_near","description":"Enemies within a radius of a point with their hp...","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"radius":{"type":"number","default":10}}},"wander":"fn run(args)
  let out = []
  for e in find_all("enemy")
    if distance(e, (0,0,0)) <= args.radius then out.push({name: e.name, hp: e.hp}) end
  end
  return {enemies: out}
end","tests":[{"args":{"radius":5},"expect":{"result":{"enemies":{"$type":"array"}}}}]}. docs/CUSTOM_TOOLS.md has recipes.

name.description: Tool name; it becomes user_<name> (lowercase, digits, underscores)

description.description: For language models: what it does, when to use it, key arguments, an example

category.description: Permission category, e.g. scene, world, custom (default custom)

input_schema.description: JSON schema of the arguments ({type: object, properties, required}); property "default"s are filled in

output_schema.description: Optional JSON schema the result must match

read_scene.description: Query entities, components and vars (default true; false runs on an empty scene)

mutate.description: Edit the scene, directly or through mutating tools (default false; needs a human's approval)

calls.description: Tools it may call (call_tool / steps), e.g. ["scene_query", "entity_*"]

capabilities.description: What the tool may do: an explicit allowlist (least privilege)

instructions.description: Wander instruction budget per call (default 1000000, max 50000000)

wander.description: kind wander: Wander code with `fn run(args) ... return {...} end` (saved to tools/<name>.wander). Builtins: call_tool, try_tool, tool_warn, tool_fail, read_file, write_file, list_files, file_exists, json_parse, json_text, tool_actor

for_each.description: Run once per element: a template giving an array, or a count

when.description: Template; the step is skipped when it is false/empty

continue_on_error.description: Keep going when this step fails

steps.description: kind composite: tool calls in order (one undo step when the tool mutates)

result.description: kind composite: result mapping template (default: the last step's result)

setup.description: Tool calls run first (rolled back with the test)

expect.description: {ok, error: code, result: subset (with $gte $lte $gt $lt $len $contains $type), contains: text, max_ms}

tests.description: Checks run by tool_define and tool_test as dry runs

from_library.description: Install a tool from the user library (tool_promote put it there)

run_tests.description: Run the tests before saving (default true); failing tests block the save

tools.name: tool_test
tools.title: Test a custom tool
tools.description: Run a custom tool's tests, or one call with "args", as a DRY RUN: scene edits are rolled back and file writes skipped, so it is safe on tools that are not approved yet. Pass "definition" (same fields as tool_define) to try a draft without saving it. Returns per-test pass/fail with the compared values, logs and timing. Example: {"name":"user_enemies_near","args":{"radius":8}}

definition.description: An unsaved definition to try instead

args.description: Run one call with these arguments instead of the tests

setup.description: With args: tool calls run first (rolled back)

filter.description: Only tests whose name contains this

tools.name: tool_list_custom
tools.title: List custom tools
tools.description: Every custom tool of the project (and external tools hosted by connected clients) with its status — active, pending_approval, rejected, disabled, offline, invalid — kind, version, author and call counts, plus the project's policy. include_library lists your user library (tool_promote); reload rescans tools/ for hand-edited definitions.

tools.name: tool_inspect
tools.title: Inspect a custom tool
tools.description: Full definition of a custom tool: code or steps, schemas, capabilities, limits, tests, status and why, approval (by whom, for which hash), stats (calls, failures, timing) and its recent calls and errors. Use it to debug a tool or before changing it.

tools.name: tool_remove
tools.title: Remove a custom tool
tools.description: Unregister a custom tool and delete its files (tools/<name>.tool.json and .wander) unless delete_files is false. External tools are unregistered until their client registers them again.

tools.name: tool_approve
tools.title: Approve a custom tool (human)
tools.description: A HUMAN approves (or rejects with approve:false) the current definition of a custom tool that needs approval (it mutates, writes files or reaches the network, or the policy is "ask"). The approval is bound to the definition's hash: changing the tool needs approval again. Agents cannot approve; ask the human to use the editor's Studio > Tools panel or `skywalker call tool_approve '{"name":"user_x"}' --project DIR`.

tools.name: tool_enable
tools.title: Enable or disable a custom tool
tools.description: Turn a custom tool off (it disappears from tools/list but keeps its files and approval) or back on.

annotations.title: Enable or disable a custom tool

tools.name: tool_promote
tools.title: Promote a tool to the user library
tools.description: Copy a project's custom tool into your user library (~/.skywalker/tools) so other projects can install it with tool_define {"from_library": "user_x"} (their approval rules apply).

annotations.title: Promote a tool to the user library

tools.name: tool_policy
tools.title: Custom tool policy
tools.description: Read or set who approves custom tools in this project (game.json customTools.policy): off (disabled), ask (every tool needs a human's approval), auto (default: read-only tools run at once, tools that mutate or write files need approval), trust (no approvals). Agents may only make it stricter.

tools.name: events_poll
tools.title: Follow engine events
tools.description: Read the engine's live event stream (the same events the editor's Activity feed shows: tool calls with their actor, studio changes such as messages, tasks, feedback, decisions and loops, play state, selection, scene loads/saves, asset changes) after a cursor, without consuming them. Pass the returned `next` as `since` on the next call; since=0 starts with everything still retained (the last 4096 events). Filter with types ("tool", "studio", "studio.message", "play_state", ...), actors (prefix match, e.g. "mcp:sky-agents") or exclude_actors. wait_ms > 0 long-polls until a matching event arrives (agent socket connections only; use a dedicated connection, the wait blocks that connection). Example: {since: 120, types: ["studio.message"], wait_ms: 20000}.

since.description: Cursor: the `next` of the previous call (0 = from the oldest retained event)

types.description: Only these event types ("type" or "type.kind", e.g. "studio.task")

actors.description: Only events whose actor starts with one of these

exclude_actors.description: Skip events whose actor starts with one of these (e.g. your own)

wait_ms.description: Long-poll: wait up to this long for a matching event (max 25000, default 0)

tools.name: tool_host_register
tools.title: Serve tools from your process
tools.description: Offer tools implemented in your own process (a Python agent harness, a script) to every agent connected to this engine: each becomes an engine tool named py_<name> that appears in tools/list. Calls are queued for you; fetch them with tool_host_poll on a dedicated connection and answer each with tool_host_reply. Keep polling: a host that has not polled for ttl_seconds (default 60) is dropped with its tools. Re-register with the returned host id to change the tool set. Example: {label: "sky-agents memory", tools: [{name: "memory_recall", description: "Search the team's shared memory", input_schema: {type: "object", properties: {query: {type: "string"}}, required: ["query"]}}]}.

description.description: What it does, for language models

mutates.description: Changes the project or game (default false)

capabilities.description: Engine tools it calls back into while serving a call: {calls: [names or globs], mutate, network} (docs/CUSTOM_TOOLS.md); callbacks pass _meta["skywalker/call_id"]

tools.description: The tools to serve

host.description: Your host id from an earlier registration (to update its tool set)

label.description: Who serves these tools, shown in descriptions and tool_host_list

ttl_seconds.description: Drop this host after this long without a poll (30-3600, default 60)

replace.description: Take over names another host serves (default false)

tools.name: tool_host_poll
tools.title: Fetch calls for your tools
tools.description: Fetch the calls other agents made to your py_* tools (see tool_host_register): [{call, tool, args, actor}]. wait_ms long-polls until a call arrives (default 20000, max 25000); use a connection dedicated to polling. Answer every call with tool_host_reply. Polling also keeps your host alive.

wait_ms.description: Wait up to this long for a call (default 20000, max 25000)

tools.name: tool_host_reply
tools.title: Answer a tool call
tools.description: Answer one call fetched with tool_host_poll. Give text (what the calling model reads), optionally structured JSON and PNG images (base64), and is_error=true when the call failed (say why in text, with a hint).

tools.name: tool_host_unregister
tools.title: Stop serving tools
tools.description: Stop serving the py_* tools of a host (they disappear from tools/list; calls still waiting fail). Hosts that stop polling expire on their own after ttl_seconds.

tools.name: tool_host_list
tools.title: Tool hosts
tools.description: Which external processes serve py_* tools: each host's label, owner (actor), tools, queued and in-flight calls, calls served and seconds since its last poll; plus the event stream's cursor range (events_poll).

tools.name: scene_audit
tools.title: Audit what the camera sees
tools.description: Quality gate before filming or screenshots (read-only, CPU, no GPU needed). Builds the frame a camera sees and reports: visible builtin PRIMITIVE meshes (cube, sphere, capsule, cylinder, plane, cone, quad, torus) with entity and screen coverage % (occlusion-aware: a ground plane hidden under terrain or water does not count); PRIMITIVE CHARACTERS (an animator / character controller / nav agent on primitive meshes, or primitive parts arranged like a body, e.g. a sphere head on a capsule) with a kit character to replace them; DEFAULT grey or UNTEXTURED materials on visible meshes; missing texture / material / HDRI files; big meshes without LODs; texel-density outliers; a default sky; lights without shadows on hero meshes. Returns `pass` and `warnings` [{severity, code, message, hint, entity}]. Views: `camera` {eye, target, fov}, several `cameras`, `camera_entity`, `view` (editor | scene), or a `sequence` (path or sequencer entity) at `times` (seconds; default: 12 evenly spaced shots). strict=true fails when primitives (or default materials) cover more than 0.1% of any view (default limit 2%); override with max_primitive_coverage (percent). stylized=true accepts flat-colored materials (a deliberate stylized look). Examples: {"view": "scene", "strict": true}, {"sequence": "sequences/hero.sequence.json", "times": [1, 4, 8], "strict": true}, {"camera": {"eye": [0, 1.7, 5], "target": [0, 1.2, 0], "fov": 40}}.

cameras.description: Several custom views [{eye, target, fov, label?}]

view.description: Editor camera (default) or the scene's primary camera

sequence.description: Sequence path (.sequence.json) or an entity with a sequencer: audit its live camera

times.description: Sequence times in seconds (default: 12 shots across it)

strict.description: Fail when primitives or default materials cover more than 0.1% of a view (showcase bar)

max_primitive_coverage.description: Primitive coverage limit in percent (default 0.1 strict, 2 otherwise)

stylized.description: Deliberately stylized look: flat-colored materials are info, not warnings

width.description: Frame width for the aspect ratio (default 1920)

resolution.description: Coverage raster width in pixels (default 320, max 1280); higher = finer coverage

details.description: Include per-view details when auditing several views (default true)

tools.name: vehicle_create
tools.title: Create vehicle
tools.description: Make a drivable car, truck or kart from a chassis entity whose wheel meshes are child entities named wheel* (wheel_fl, wheel_fr, wheel_rl, wheel_rr; or pass `wheels`). One undoable edit that adds: a dynamic body (chassis mass), a box collider fitted to the chassis above the wheels, the `vehicle` component from a preset (sports, hatchback, truck, kart) in a handling style (arcade = traction control, ABS, drift assist, roll protection; sim = raw), a chase camera on the scene camera, a looping engine sound pitched by rpm, and the drive input actions (throttle W/Up/right trigger, brake+reverse S/Down/left trigger, steer A-D/arrows/left stick, handbrake Space/A). Forward is -Z. Wheels are fitted from their meshes and spin, steer and follow the suspension while playing. Then: vehicle_test_drive for numbers, vehicle_tune to adjust, vehicle_info capture=true to see suspension and tire forces. Example: {"entity": "Coupe", "preset": "sports"}.

entity.description: The chassis (root of the car model)

wheels.description: Wheel entities (children of the chassis); default: children named wheel*

overrides.description: vehicle component fields to set on top of the preset

chase_camera.description: Make the scene camera a chase camera following this vehicle (default true)

engine_sound.description: Add a looping engine sound pitched by rpm (default true)

input_actions.description: Add the drive input actions to the project's input map if missing (default true)

collider.description: auto = box fitted to the chassis above the wheels (default); keep = your own

tools.name: vehicle_tune
tools.title: Tune vehicle
tools.description: Change a vehicle's handling parameters with validation (one undoable edit; works while playing: the vehicle is rebuilt keeping its speed). `set` takes vehicle component fields, e.g. {"maxTorque": 600, "lateralGrip": 1.6, "antiRollRear": 12000, "driftAssist": 0.5}; unknown fields fail with a did-you-mean. `preset` + `handling` re-apply a preset first. `wheels` overrides per axle or wheel ({"rear": {"lateralGrip": 1.2}, "front_left": {...}}): the wheel list is written out from the current fit the first time. `test` (a maneuver: accel, braking, slalom, skidpad, all) drives before and after the change and returns both summaries, so you can tune by numbers. Run vehicle_test_drive for details.

wheels.description: Per-wheel overrides keyed by axle (front, rear) or wheel name (front_left, rear_right, axle1_left): {lateralGrip, longitudinalGrip, suspensionFrequency, suspensionDamping, brakeTorque, steer, drive, ...}

test.description: Measure this maneuver before and after the change

tools.name: vehicle_info
tools.title: Vehicle telemetry
tools.description: Live state of vehicles: speed (km/h), rpm, gear, inputs as asked and as applied after assists (steering smoothing, auto reverse, traction control, ABS, drift assist), drift angle, lateral/longitudinal g, and per wheel: suspension length/compression, contact point and surface, load (N), drive and cornering forces, slip ratio and slip angle, skid 0..1. While editing it shows the fitted setup at rest (wheel roles, radii) and build warnings. capture=true adds an image with the vehicles debug view (suspension rays, contacts, tire force vectors). Without `entity` it lists every vehicle. Pair with sim_control step / sim_input to watch a maneuver.

capture.description: Add a picture with the vehicles debug view (default false)

tools.name: vehicle_test_drive
tools.title: Test drive
tools.description: An autopilot drives a copy of the vehicle through standard maneuvers in a private physics world (the scene is not changed; works while editing) and returns handling metrics to tune by numbers: accel (0-60, 0-100 km/h, quarter mile, wheelspin, upshifts), braking (distance and g from `speed`, default 100 km/h; ABS activity, stability), slalom (8 cones every cone_spacing m at `speed`, default 60: completed, cones hit, average speed, line error), skidpad (circle of `radius` m, speed ramps until the car leaves the line: max lateral g, and whether it understeers, oversteers or runs out of power), top_speed (`duration` s), custom (`inputs` keyframes [{t, throttle, brake, steer, handbrake}]), all (accel, braking, slalom, skidpad). track=proving_ground (default: flat, full grip, comparable between cars) or scene (the level as it is). `overrides` tries vehicle fields without editing (e.g. {"lateralGrip": 1.6}). trace=true adds a sampled trace. Example: {"entity": "Coupe", "maneuver": "all"}.

speed.description: km/h: braking start (100), slalom (60), skidpad start (30)

inputs.description: custom: keyframes {t, throttle, brake, steer, handbrake}

overrides.description: vehicle fields for this drive only

trace.description: Include a trace sampled every 0.25 s

tools.name: particles2d_create
tools.title: Create 2D particles
tools.description: Create pixel-art particles for a 2D game from a preset, ready to tweak: rain (streaks over the whole view), drizzle, snow (drifting flakes), leaves and petals (falling, swaying), fireflies (glowing, twinkling, wandering), smoke (chimney puffs), ripples (puddle rings while it rains), dust (motes in sunlight), sparkle (water glints). Weather presets (rain, drizzle, snow, ripples) wrap: their box tiles endlessly so they fill whatever the camera shows, wherever the entity is. Untextured particles are solid pixel rectangles (`pixelSize` texels); give a `texture` sheet (with `columns`/`rows`, `frames`, `animate` random|life|loop) for leaves, flakes or ripple rings. `overrides` patches fields, e.g. {"rate": 400, "color": "#9fc4ff", "pixelsPerUnit": 16}. Simulated on fixed ticks while playing (deterministic, reset on stop). Example: particles2d_create {"preset": "fireflies", "position": [12, 4, 0], "overrides": {"area": [14, 6]}}.

position.description: World position (center of the emission box)

tools.name: particles2d_info
tools.title: 2D particle stats
tools.description: Live state of particles2d emitters: particles alive, cap, rate, box, wrap, and the bounds the live particles cover (world units). Use it to check that weather is running while playing, or to find emitters that hit their maxParticles cap. Without `entity` lists every emitter in the scene.
